title: HTML, CSS & JavaScript
theory: HTML describes meaningful structure. CSS controls presentation. JavaScript reacts to events and changes state or the DOM. A good interface remains understandable with keyboard navigation and clear labels.

Form values start as text. Parse and validate them intentionally. For displaying untrusted text, use textContent rather than inserting it as executable markup. Browser-side checks improve usability but do not replace server-side validation.

Test clicking, keyboard activation, empty inputs, repeat submissions, and resizing. State the expected behavior of each control. A preview is a way to inspect behavior, not an automatic accessibility certification.

The HTML preview here is sandboxed and cannot access your account or the parent page. Network requests and external assets are disabled. Keep HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in one file for preview labs; use local project files for multi-file applications.

quiz.prompt: Which is responsible for document structure?
quiz.explanation: HTML defines the document and its semantic elements.

quiz.prompt: A button should run code when activated. Attach what?
quiz.explanation: An event listener connects an event to a handler.

quiz.prompt: Which is appropriate for showing an untrusted label as plain text?
quiz.explanation: textContent treats the value as text rather than markup.

quiz.prompt: A form input value is normally what type?
Why must a server validate values already checked by JavaScript?
options: Clients can bypass or alter client-side checks
quiz.explanation: The server must not trust a client to enforce its rules.

quiz.prompt: A usable form field should have?
quiz.explanation: A persistent associated label identifies the input clearly.
